note: Synthetic, author-written batches (no real conversations). Each batch may contain several independent enduring statements plus noise the extractor must ignore. gold: every term must appear in one proposal's claim. forbid: a proposal containing all these terms is a false positive.

cases.text: From now on write commit messages in the imperative mood. Always run the linter before committing. I prefer small pull requests. Use tabs, never spaces, in Go files.

I always write tests before the implementation. Which database would you pick here? If I had unlimited budget I would buy a bigger cluster. Please keep answers short, I prefer bullet lists over prose. Remember that I deploy only on Tuesdays.
My manager insists on weekly reports. I prefer dark mode in every editor. Forget that I mentioned my cat, don't store it. I like reading release notes before upgrading.
I prefer snake_case for Python names. I always pin dependency versions. I like keeping functions under thirty lines. I want TODO comments to carry a ticket id. I prefer squash merges.
Which framework is better for this? Say I had a week off, I would learn Rust. My teammate loves Vim. I skimmed a post about GraphQL today. Maybe I will try tabs for a bit, not sure yet.
I am deeply interested in compilers and type systems. I have ten years of experience with PostgreSQL tuning. My goal this year is to ship a database engine in Rust.
I prefer tabs for indentation. Actually, scratch that: I want two spaces, never tabs. Also, I prefer concise commit subjects under fifty characters.
Give me the command first and the explanation after. Ask before running anything destructive. This once, skip the tests, we are in a hurry.
Just for this repo, always run make check before opening a PR. Also in this repo I prefer rebasing over merge commits.
